sections.h2: Ways to sell a Perry house
sections.html:
You can list with a realtor, sell on your own, or take an offer from a cash investor. The right pick comes down to repairs, your calendar and how much you want to deal with showings.

Perry draws buyers from two directions. Robins Air Force Base anchors the local job market, and Interstate 75 carries commuters and travelers through town. A tidy, well-placed house can appeal to both groups. A house with a leaking roof, an unclosed permit, a probate problem or a tenant who won't leave sits longer, and owners of those houses often call an investor first.

  • Realtor listing: the widest exposure and often the highest price, along with open houses, inspection haggling and a closing date set by the buyer's bank.
  • Private sale: you keep the commission and take on pricing, contracts and every question a buyer raises.
  • Investor purchase: no repairs, a fast closing, and a price that usually lands below a polished listing.

Get each proposal in writing. A higher asking price can shrink after commissions, repairs and the extra months of taxes and upkeep you carry while you wait.

Perry has 25,699 residents as of July 2025, up from 20,624 at the 2020 count and 13,839 in 2010. Growth tied to Robins Air Force Base began in the early 1940s, and the oldest houses stand near the courthouse square, where a buyer's inspector will study roofs, wiring and plumbing closely. The east side along Perry Parkway was built out later, so sellers on opposite sides of town are often dealing with homes of very different ages.

sections.h2: City of Perry permits and code rules
sections.html:
Community Development is the city department for permits, inspections, planning and code compliance. Permit submittals go through an online portal and attachments must be PDFs. A state contractor who has never pulled a Perry permit is asked to phone the department first.

  • Staff decisions: sign permits, building permits, site plans, final plats, minor subdivisions and zoning compliance, plus a certificate of appropriateness for work in historic districts.
  • Planning Commission items: variances, administrative appeals, preliminary plats, special exceptions, rezonings and map or text amendments, each with a staff report.
  • Code Compliance: handles complaints about derelict vehicles, illegal signs, overgrown grass, and trash or debris under the city's Chapter 19 on nuisances.

Before you name a price, ask Community Development what its file shows for your address: an open complaint or an unclosed permit is easier to clear now than at the closing table. An investor can absorb those loose ends, but the offer will reflect them.

sections.h2: How do Houston County property taxes affect a Perry sale?
sections.html:
The county Tax Assessor sets the valuation and the Tax Commissioner sends the bill. Each keeps a Perry office in the courthouse at 201 Perry Parkway.

The bill rests on a January 1 valuation, a 40% assessment ratio and a millage rate. One mill is a dollar for every thousand dollars of assessed value. Ask for the current bill and any open balance on your parcel before closing, because the settlement agent will want both.

• Homestead exemption: the owner files the first application with the Tax Assessor by April 1 of the first year it is claimed. It carries forward until the owner changes or switches exemptions.
  • Appeal window: 45 days from receipt of a notice of changed value.
  • Appeal path: the assessors review first, then the Board of Equalization or arbitration, and then court.

Valid grounds are whether the property is taxable, what it is worth, and whether that worth lines up with similar parcels. The size of the tax bill itself cannot be appealed. A homestead exemption does not travel with the house: when the deed passes, the buyer files fresh. The Tax Assessor's office can be reached at (478) 218-4750.

sections.h2: Recording the deed and the transfer tax
sections.html:
A Georgia deed sits unrecorded until its transfer tax is paid. The tax is an excise on the sale, separate from property tax, and it is reported on Form PT-61. You fill out the form on the GSCCCA website and print it to file with the deed. Each deed takes one PT-61.

In Perry the recording office is the Houston County clerk's office. Your settlement agent normally files both papers. The purchase contract decides who pays the tax, and the agent can confirm the rate for your deed.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale suit a Perry house?
sections.html:
A cash sale fits when speed and certainty count for more than top dollar. Perry owners tend to consider it for these situations:

  • An inherited house that nobody plans to occupy and that needs a full clean-out.
  • Repairs that would swallow more cash than the owner wants to spend before listing.
  • A mortgage in arrears with a lender deadline approaching.
  • A rental with turnover or tenant trouble the owner no longer wants to manage.
  • A code complaint or lapsed permit likely to slow a financed buyer's inspection.

Have the price, the closing day and the split of costs on paper, then set that beside what a listing would net.

sections.h2: Steps before you accept an offer
sections.html:
1. Pull your parcel's current tax bill and any open balance from the Tax Commissioner.
  2. Ask Community Development whether any permit or complaint is still open on the address.
  3. Decide which repair requests you would grant and which you would refuse.
  4. Collect at least one cash offer and one agent's opinion of value in writing.
  5. Choose a settlement agent early, so the PT-61 and the deed are ready when you sign.

Tax questions go to the county offices in the courthouse. Questions about liens or title go to your settlement agent.

faqs.q: Can a Perry house sell in any condition?
faqs.a: Yes. An investor takes the house in whatever state it is in, while a retail buyer may press for repairs after inspection. Decide beforehand which repair requests you would accept and which you would refuse.

faqs.q: Whom do I call about a Perry property value?
faqs.a: Call the Houston County Tax Assessor in the courthouse at 201 Perry Parkway, at (478) 218-4750. The Tax Commissioner, who sends the bills, keeps a Perry office at the same address.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to contest a new value on a Perry parcel?
faqs.a: Forty-five days after you receive the notice of change. Send a written appeal to the assessors. If they hold the value, the file moves to the Board of Equalization, or you can choose arbitration instead.

faqs.q: Does a homestead exemption stay with a house after a sale?
faqs.a: No. Houston County renews an exemption automatically only for the same owner, so a change of ownership ends it. The new owner applies by April 1 of the first year they want the exemption.

faqs.q: What filings record a Perry sale?
faqs.a: A deed plus Form PT-61 go to the Houston County clerk's office once the transfer tax is paid. The PT-61 is filled out on the GSCCCA site, and the settlement agent usually handles both.
